prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core purpose
- Stand for Scotland’s independence and strengthened powers for the Scottish Parliament. Electing more SNP MPs pushes a referendum; a majority would trigger one. SNP MPs will always prioritise Scotland’s interests and oppose anti-Scottish measures.

Economic strategy and public investment
- Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations using surplus oil revenues to provide a permanent income stream for services (benchmark 8% real return; long-term aim >£1bn/yr).
- Establish a Scottish Trust for Public Investment (STPI) to finance infrastructure more cheaply than PFI/PPP, freeing resources for schools, hospitals, transport and housing.
- Comprehensive Review of Taxation to deliver fairness and simplicity without raising the overall tax burden; initial step: cut fuel duty by 10p/gal funded by a new 5p income tax band above £100,000.
- Promoteenterprise, broadband access nationwide, streamlined development agencies, stronger global marketing of Scotland; integrate tourism into enterprise strategy.

Constitution and governance
- Written constitution, inclusive citizenship, Queen retained as Head of State subject to referendum. Proportional representation at all levels. Cut quangos and increase accountability. Civil service opportunities under independence.

Education and young people
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow. Establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18, end league tables, cut assessment burden; major school refurbishment via STPI. Expand Gaelic-medium education; protect rural schools; promote Scots and Scottish history.

Jobs, wages and unions
- Devolve and refocus New Deal into a “Better Deal,” emphasising reskilling. Raise minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages, with support for small businesses. Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU employee protections.

Health and care
- Create a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment; HTBS drug/treatment approvals binding. Free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges. Invest in equipment, 1,500 more nurses, a Clean Hospitals Fund; aim to halve inpatient waiting times in first term. Free personal care for the elderly.

Environment, energy, water
- Lead on sustainability; oppose UK climate levy’s impact on hydro. Target 12% of total energy (including 25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear, plan decommissioning expertise at Dounreay. Promote the “six Rs.” Reform water charging, halt backdoor privatisation, democratise water bodies.

Europe and defence
- Pro-EU, anti-superstate; stronger subsidiarity and national vetoes on resources, tax and constitution. Euro entry only with the right conditions and referendum. Remove Trident from Scotland; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased withdrawal from NATO while maintaining conventional cooperation; form a professional Scottish Defence Force.

Social justice, housing and communities
- National Anti-Poverty Strategy; fair, fast asylum processes; devolve equalities powers. Address local authority housing debt; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfers. Support voluntary sector core funding; tackle homelessness.

Law, order and drugs
- Fund 1,000 additional police officers. Expand drug courts and rehabilitation. Parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifetime supervision for high-risk sex offenders; speed up lower court cases.

Pensions and social security
- Restore earnings link for state pensions; spread winter fuel payments weekly; review interactions with MIG; streamline benefits delivery in a single agency; simplify housing benefit; improve disability support; consider winter fuel for severely disabled under-60s.

Transport
- Ensure fair UK investment share; create Regional Transport Authorities; public stake in Railtrack; reopen key lines, electrify priority routes, expand airport and ferry access, national concessionary travel; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Cut fuel duty; improve rural transport and ICT; protect key services; compensate crisis-hit businesses. Post–foot-and-mouth review; avoid early “gold-plating” of EU rules; promote diversification and organics. Reform the CFP, decentralise management, support tie-up schemes and processing; independent salmon farming inquiry.

Culture, broadcasting and sport
- Devolve broadcasting; support “Scottish Six” and digital rollout. Reform arts funding, create a national theatre and “Scottish Academy,” consider a Scottish Lottery. Focus sports funding on communities; develop football academies; bid for Euro 2008.
